question:
Patient note:
A 35-year-old man is evaluated this morning in the orthopedic pre-operative suite in anticipation of a left total knee replacement that the surgical team predicts will take roughly two hours under regional-plus-general anesthesia with an expected three-night hospital stay on the joint reconstruction ward. The knee has deteriorated over the past year following a remote meniscal injury sustained while playing amateur soccer; over the last six weeks crepitus, locking, and sharp weight-bearing pain have progressed to the point that, aside from assisted toileting, he has remained in bed or reclined on a sofa continuously for the past four days, relying on his partner for meals and transfers. He arrives today on a wheeled stretcher because he cannot tolerate even a few steps with crutches without severe discomfort. Review of recent events reveals that 18 days ago he underwent an uncomplicated open reduction and internal fixation of a right distal radius fracture after a cycling crash; that procedure was performed at an outside facility under general anesthesia, and the surgical wound is healing well without signs of infection or hardware failure. During that admission he received no blood products and was discharged on postoperative day two with oral analgesics and instructions for early wrist mobilization. His past medical history is otherwise notable for a symptomatic deep venous thrombosis in the left popliteal segment three years ago that developed during a trans-Pacific flight; duplex ultrasonography at that time confirmed occlusive clot, and he completed six months of rivaroxaban with interval imaging documenting full recanalization. Further hematologic work-up then demonstrated heterozygosity for the Factor V Leiden mutation, a finding subsequently confirmed on two separate occasions; he has not been maintained on long-term anticoagulation since completing the therapeutic course, and he has never experienced a pulmonary embolus, arterial thrombus, or transient ischemic attack. He denies malignancy, bowel disease, chronic lung conditions, myocardial infarction, congestive heart failure, systemic infection, recent fevers, or respiratory symptoms beyond mild seasonal rhinorrhea. No one in his first-degree family has suffered unexplained clotting events, and his three siblings have declined genetic testing. He does not smoke, drinks beer socially, and has never used intravenous or recreational drugs. Medications taken until yesterday include ibuprofen 600 mg every six hours as needed, acetaminophen-hydrocodone two tablets nightly for sleep, and an over-the-counter glucosamine-chondroitin supplement; he stopped all nonsteroidal anti-inflammatories 72 hours before today’s procedure per anesthesia instructions and takes no hormones, steroids, erythropoiesis-stimulating agents, or antiplatelet drugs. Physical examination finds an alert, well-developed man lying supine, conversant, and in no acute distress. Vital signs: temperature 36.6 °C, blood pressure 122/70 mm Hg, heart rate 74 beats/min regular, respiratory rate 14 breaths/min, and oxygen saturation 98 % on ambient air. Airway assessment reveals Mallampati class I with full cervical range of motion and intact dentition. Cardiac auscultation demonstrates a crisp S1 and S2 without murmurs, gallops, or rubs; jugular venous pulsation is at 3 cm H₂O, and peripheral pulses are 2+ and symmetrical. Lungs are clear to auscultation with good air entry and no adventitious sounds. Abdominal examination is benign with active bowel sounds, a soft, nontender contour, and no organomegaly. The left knee appears swollen and valgus-deformed with diffuse joint line tenderness, crepitus on passive flexion beyond 45°, and range limited to 60°; there is no erythema or warmth. Calf circumferences are equal, the skin is warm and of normal color, and no cords, varicosities, or pitting edema are present. The contralateral lower limb shows full, pain-free motion and no effusion. Examination of the right forearm discloses a 6-cm linear scar over the volar aspect with well-approximated staples, no drainage, and intact distal neurovascular status. Neurologic testing reveals 5/5 strength in upper extremities and the right lower extremity, intact sensation, and brisk symmetric reflexes. No indwelling central venous catheters, ports, or peripherally inserted lines are present; intravenous access today is via a single 18-gauge cannula placed in the dorsum of the right hand by nursing staff. Laboratory data obtained two hours ago include hemoglobin 15.0 g/dL, hematocrit 45 %, platelets 238 × 10⁹/L, leukocytes 6.2 × 10⁹/L, sodium 140 mmol/L, potassium 4.2 mmol/L, creatinine 0.9 mg/dL, AST 24 U/L, ALT 21 U/L, total bilirubin 0.7 mg/dL, prothrombin time 12.3 s with an INR of 1.0, and activated partial thromboplastin time 29 s. An electrocardiogram demonstrates normal sinus rhythm at 72 beats/min without conduction delays or repolarization abnormalities, and a pre-operative upright chest radiograph is clear. Plain knee radiographs reviewed by the orthopedic attending show tri-compartmental joint-space narrowing, subchondral sclerosis, and osteophyte formation consistent with end-stage degenerative change. Sequential compression sleeves have been ordered but have remained off while final consents are signed. He has been nil per os since midnight, last voided without difficulty an hour ago, and consents to neuraxial blockade plus a general anesthetic. The peri-operative medicine service is consulted to assist with risk mitigation in the context of his inherited prothrombotic tendency, remote thrombotic episode, recent operative history, and several days of near-complete immobility.

Question: What is the patient's Caprini Score for Venous Thromboembolism?
solution:
Apply the Caprini surgical VTE risk score before knee replacement:
- Planned elective lower-extremity arthroplasty: total knee replacement = 5. Do not also score its operative duration as major surgery.
- Personal history of VTE: confirmed popliteal DVT = 3, even though the clot resolved.
- Known thrombophilia: heterozygous Factor V Leiden = 3, independent of the prior DVT.
- Bed confinement for >72 hours: four days with transfers only for toileting = 2.
- Major surgery within the past month: open fixation of the wrist fracture 18 days ago = 1. This was a separate operation.
- Age 35 = 0; no other scored factors are documented.
Total = 5 + 3 + 3 + 2 + 1 = 14.
Final answer: 14
